newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank ups whole German banking sector to buy.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank ups whole German banking sector to buy.

text.p: Commerzbank AG on Monday issued a "buy" recommendation on all of Germany's major banking shares as a result of the merger plans announced by Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechsel-Bank AG.
"This is the first major merger in the German commerical banking sector," said banking analyst Dieter Hein.
"It means the speculation about future merger moves can only continue, particularly for smaller banks," he said.
The recommendation affects all five DAX-listed bank shares and BHF Bank AG.
Commerzbank previously had a hold recommendation on Dresdner Bank AG and Hypo-Bank while it recommended buying other banking shares.
"The important point is that this is positive for the whole sector," said Hein.
Hein said the merger between Vereinsbank and Hypo would reduce the total number of their shares in circulation and thus substantially increase earnings per share.
In addition, the markets would be impressed by the banks' plans to save through synergies.
Preliminary estimates indicated an earnings per share of five marks in 1997 for the merged bank, he said.
Hein said the merger plan was not likely to raise cartel authority concerns.
Allianz AG will own 15 percent of the new bank, as well as more than 20 percent of Dresdner Bank AG, hitherto Germany's second largest bank.
"The problems would start if Allianz had more than 25 percent (of the merged bank)," he said.
For Dresdner Bank, the news means a fall-off in some merger speculation that had become attached to it over the past year.
"The talk was very much that Dresdner and Hypo could get together because of the fact that they share a major shareholder. That of course is gone now," Hein said.
